headline: Committee discusses 2026 storm recovery, SBA loans and Kīhei gulch sediment; item deferred

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.summary: The committee took up DRIP 9.4 on long-term recovery from the 2026 storms, including SBA loans, 92 damaged County sites and about $100 million in damages. The item was deferred without objection.
meeting.recap: The committee's only item was DRIP 9.4, Maui's long-term recovery operations, focused on recovery from the 2026 storms.[[0:06:03]] The deadline was June 14, but late applications are accepted until August 13.[[0:11:22]] SBA has approved 170 loans, for over $11 million.[[0:16:19]] No loan payments are due until 12 months after the first payout.[[0:16:52]] SBA opened a loan help center in Kīhei, open Monday through Friday, 9 to 6.[[0:17:20]] About 300,000 cubic yards of sediment in the Kīhei gulches needs to be removed.[[0:28:43]] FEMA (the federal disaster agency) left parks facilities out of reimbursement, and the state has appealed.[[0:34:37]] A request for more than $20 million to clear three gulches is with the USDA.[[0:52:20]] A structural review of a storm-damaged gym is expected within about 60 days.[[1:16:55]] Officials agreed to send a follow-up letter about a detention basin issue the chair raised.[[1:47:34]] The item was deferred without objection.[[1:52:57]]
meeting.next: The County is doing more site inspections with FEMA, then will send a final damage report to FEMA. Officials expect to come back sometime in fiscal 27 with a budget amendment to cover the funding need. A follow-up letter will go to Public Works about the detention basin issue.

moments.q: "So please remember to tell people that homeowners and renters are eligible for loans."
Map of storm damage: "every circle on there represents damaged infrastructure that the county owns"
